newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Schroders to make strong H1 showing.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Schroders to make strong H1 showing.

text.p: British investment bank Schroders Plc is expected to make a strong showing when it reports its first half results next week, banking sector analysts said.
One analyst, who asked not to be named, said he was very positive for the interim stage and expected to upgrade his full-year forecast of 235 million stg.

A Reuters survey of analysts' forecasts gave a range of 106 to 125 million stg for pre-tax profit, a consensus of 115 million stg. The consensus dividend forecast was 5.0 pence, with a range of 5.0-6.0 pence. Pre-tax profit for the same period in 1995 was 85.6 million stg, and the dividend 4.5 pence.
"It's a good, sound investment bank that we expect to continue to do well," another analyst said.
The first analyst said Schroders' fund management arm would drive its performance, pointing to the showings of other fund management groups such as Invesco.
It was harder to judge on the bank's investment banking, although mergers and acquisitions volumes were higher in the first quarter and lower in the second quarter, he added.
The second analyst said the performance of other investment banks and the generally buoyant underlying market for their services and products should underpin Schroders' performance.
On the recurring question of the bank's independence, analysts were split on whether it would remain as one of the last bastions of the British merchant banking sector.

They agreed the bank, which has a controlling family holding, wants to remain indepedent, even though regularly cited as a bid target and often thought of as a potential candidate for demerging its banking and fund management arms.
One said he thought it would not hang on to its independence for more than another two years by which time the desire for additional capital for its investment banking arm would become overwhelming.
This could either lead to a full-scale merger or a tie up like the one brokered between Rothschilds and ABN Amro.
Another said Schroders presented an expensive target as it stood as the family interest was an obstacle that would be hard to get around. "I don't think it's up for grabs," he said.
In March Schroders reported record full-year pre-tax profits of 197.3 million stg. It said costs were under control, despite a rise in expenses.
It will report is interim figures on Friday, September 6.
